channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Strikes between U.S. and Iran continue as hostilities intensify
item.description: The U.S. has launched more strikes at Iran, one day after the two countries exchanged fire for the first time in a month

item.title: Ex-National Security Council advisor on the latest strikes between the U.S. and Iran
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks retired Rear Admiral and Biden administration National Security Council advisor John Kirby about the latest exchange of fire between the U.S. and Iran.

item.title: He died of 'natural causes.' But his mother says she knows what killed him: heat
item.description: When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.
item.content:encoded:
When Arizona counts heat-related deaths, Adam Willson isn't included. His story shows how thousands of heat deaths can go uncounted every year in the United States.

item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: U.S. military strikes rock Iran for a second day in a row, Trump attempts to combat rising gas prices as midterm approaches, Sen. Ed Markey wins Massachusetts' Democratic primary.

item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with journalist and author Rozina Ali about her new book, "Seasons of Fury: Four Families and the Rise of Islamophobia in America."

item.title: Whistleblower claims USPS plan for Trump's mail voting order could disrupt midterms
item.description: An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint that a technical system the Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed and, if implemented, likely to disrupt the fall midterms.
item.content:encoded: An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint that a technical system the Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed and, if implemented, likely to disrupt the fall midterms.
item.dc:creator: Hansi Lo Wang

item.title: Whistleblower's lawyer warns USPS plan for Trump's order could keep ballots from voters
item.description: A lawyer for an anonymous whistleblower says Postal Service plans for an unusual verification rule, combined with a hastily built online system, could delay mail ballots from reaching eligible voters.
item.content:encoded:
A lawyer for an anonymous whistleblower says Postal Service plans for an unusual verification rule, combined with a hastily built online system, could delay mail ballots from reaching eligible voters.

(Image credit: David Zalubowski)
item.dc:creator: Steve Inskeep

item.title: Advocates say cities' aggressive clearing of encampments has caused more problems
item.description: A Supreme Court ruling two years ago allowed bans on sleeping outside. Homeless people and advocates in the Midwest say aggressive encampment clearing has caused problems.
